attempts.reason_tested: marker is in the severity label / confounded by anaemia (DS07)
attempts.method: Read /experiments/shared/tidy/DS07.outcomes.json (complicated = any of collapse, cerebral signs, death < 24 h, haematocrit < 0.15 or > 0.5, urea, creatinine, bilirubin > 30, glucose, lactate, band neutrophils > 1.5). Checked DS07.features.json for any haematocrit, bilirubin or haemolysis-index variable. Recomputed haemoglobin beta (P60524) complicated vs uncomplicated with within-plex permutation and bootstrap by dog (script /experiments/SV-META/refutation/scripts/K03_checks.py, seed 20261112). Also compared uncomplicated dogs with healthy controls.
attempts.result: Reproduced: Cliff +0.476, within-plex permutation p 0.02, bootstrap 95% CI +0.09 to +0.81 (14 vs 18). DS07 has no haematocrit, bilirubin or haemolysis index, so haemoglobin beta cannot be expressed 'per unit of anaemia'; the candidate's central quantity is not measured in either source. The label contains haematocrit < 0.15 and bilirubin > 30, both haemolysis consequences, so a dog can be 'complicated' because it haemolysed more; the contrast is partly circular. Uncomplicated infected dogs equal healthy controls (Cliff -0.006), although all B. rossi dogs haemolyse. Not a formal rejection alone because the label variables are not in the file, but it removes the 'per unit of anaemia' interpretation.

attempts.reason_tested: sample (ex vivo) haemolysis or a shared pre-analytical factor (DS07)
attempts.method: Same script. Correlated haemoglobin beta with another erythrocyte cytosolic protein (peroxiredoxin 2, F1PCG4; carbonic anhydrase 2 had only 6 dogs) and with the neutrophil/monocyte proteins lactoferrin (F1PR54) and CD14 (A0A1S7J0A8); tested the haemoglobin-beta/PRDX2 log ratio; adjusted haemoglobin beta for lactoferrin, CD14, haptoglobin and albumin by rank residuals, then repeated the within-plex permutation.
attempts.result: PRDX2 is also higher in complicated dogs (Cliff +0.74, p 0.006, 9 vs 13) and moves with haemoglobin beta (rho +0.77); the HBB/PRDX2 ratio does not differ (Cliff +0.16, p 0.45). The signal is therefore 'more red-cell content in serum', which in vivo intravascular lysis and ex vivo lysis of archived serum produce alike; no haemolysis index exists to separate them. Adjusted for lactoferrin the effect falls to +0.24 (p 0.16), for CD14 to +0.30 (p 0.11): the haemoglobin signal is not separable from the neutrophil/monocyte axis that shares a pre-analytical or disease-intensity source (SV-06 report b.5). Adjusted for haptoglobin it rises (+0.57, p 0.002; HBB-Hp log ratio +0.62, p 0.0008), the one result that points to more haemoglobin per scavenger; adjusted for albumin +0.40 (p 0.044). Artefact not proven, but not excluded.

attempts.reason_tested: fragility: result rests on a few dogs
attempts.method: Same script: sorted haemoglobin beta by group; removed the 3 highest complicated dogs and repeated the within-plex test.
attempts.result: 5 of 14 complicated dogs lie above the highest uncomplicated value; 6 complicated dogs are at or below the uncomplicated median. Without the top 3 complicated dogs Cliff +0.33, p 0.12. The effect comes from a high-haemoglobin minority, compatible either with a haemolytic minority or with a few grossly haemolysed samples.

attempts.reason_tested: DS02 contrast is parasite load (dose sets load) and already published
attempts.method: Same script: pre-treatment cfHb (mg/L), parasitaemia and haematocrit per Beagle from /experiments/shared/tidy/DS02.features.json; died from DS02.outcomes.json. Read the CB082 note and full text (/core/data/markdown/CB082.md) for plasma haemoglobin by inoculum.
attempts.result: Peak cfHb ranks exactly with peak parasitaemia (Spearman +1.0, n 5: low dose 70 and 100 mg/L at 4.7 and 6.8%; high dose 230, 580, 1560 at 35, 46, 60%) and with the haematocrit fall (+0.9). The dog that died (d003) had 580 mg/L on day 3 (day-4 value missing), lower than a survivor (d002, 1560). cfHb per % parasitaemia on the same day is about 22 (low dose, day 4) and 26 to 41 (high dose, days 3-4), with one value of 3; no consistent excess per unit of load. Exact p 0.2 is the minimum possible with 3 vs 2. CB082 (10.1186/s12864-021-07889-4) already reports that plasma haemoglobin rose earlier in the high-inoculum cohort and that severity scaled with dose. The SRC-B indicator is a load effect and a published finding; it gives no independent support for 'more haemolysis per unit of anaemia'.

DS07 haemoglobin beta q 0.133 in its family of 10 (does not pass 0.05). T04 Stouffer p 0.005, BH q 0.010 over 8 themes, but the themes were chosen after the results were seen (note in themes.csv), and leave-one-source-out max p 0.1. With SRC-B reduced to a load effect (attempt 4), the theme rests on one source with q 0.133. The combined statistic does not stand.

attempts.reason_tested: canine severity data already exist (gap claim)
attempts.method: grep of /core/articles/*.md and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md for cell-free/free/plasma/serum haemoglobin, haemoglobinaemia, haemoglobinuria, haemopexin, haem oxygenase, haemoconcentration; read CB082, CB412, CB187, CB325, CB040, CB119, CB157, CB053, CB025 contexts. PubMed: '(babesiosis OR Babesia) AND (dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (haemoglobinaemia OR hemoglobinemia OR "free hemoglobin" OR "plasma hemoglobin" OR "cell-free hemoglobin" OR "free haemoglobin")' (5 hits) and '(babesiosis OR Babesia) AND (dog OR canine) AND (haemoglobinuria OR hemoglobinuria OR haptoglobin OR hemopexin OR haemoconcentration OR hemoconcentration) AND (outcome OR mortality OR severity OR complicated OR death)' (17 hits).
attempts.result: No in-window CB article relates a measured cfHb, haemopexin or haem load to death or complicated status in natural canine babesiosis. Close existing data: CB325 (10.4102/jsava.v77i4.373) and CB412 (10.1016/j.tvjl.2011.01.027) measured free serum haemoglobin in babesiosis vs controls and against urea (median 1.3 vs 0.8 g/L in CB412), not against severity; CB082 (10.1186/s12864-021-07889-4) plasma haemoglobin by dose (experimental); CB157 summarises Polish B. canis work in which free haemoglobin did not relate to urea or creatinine rise (a canine organ-dysfunction null, primary sources not checked); CB040 (10.1016/j.vetpar.2019.06.005) haemoconcentrated cases with obvious haemolysis, 3 of 4 died, though the authors attribute haemoconcentration to plasma leak; CB119 cites an odds ratio of 32.7 for haemoconcentrating disease and calls cfHb a potential severity measure (proposed, not measured); CB187 analysed haemoglobinuria by invasion intensity (abstract only). Pre-window: experimental haemoglobinaemia did not cause significant nephropathy in dogs (Lobetti 1996, PMID 9284030, no DOI). The gap for quantified cfHb or haem load against outcome in natural disease holds; the 'haemolysis without anaemia is bad' clinical observation (haemoconcentration) already exists in CB040/CB119, and the AKI arm has canine nulls.

attempts.method: Read /core/data/markdown/HU002.md, HU003.md, HU010.md; PubMed metadata for PMID 23314583.
attempts.result: Verified: HU002 severe falciparum malaria, AKI patients had higher cfHb (geometric mean 8.8 vs 5.1 uM, p 0.018) and cfHb correlated with parasite burden (10.1186/s12879-017-2373-1). HU003 Ugandan children: haemin and cfHb at presentation associated with mortality (p < 0.05) and haemopexin lower in severe malaria (10.1186/s12936-015-1028-1). HU010 knowlesi malaria: cfHb increased with severity and was associated with parasitaemia (10.1038/s41426-018-0105-2). Sepsis: higher cfHb independently associated with in-hospital death, OR 1.078 (10.1097/CCM.0b013e3182741a54). Direction agrees; note that in malaria cfHb also tracks parasite burden, the same load confounding seen in DS02.

attempts.method: Grid rows F1-01 to F1-05 in /experiments/SV-06/a/out/transfer_grid.csv; CB325, CB412, DS02 variable definitions; CB117, CB476 notes.
attempts.result: Canine cfHb has been measured spectrophotometrically (CB325, CB412; DS02 'CFHb' in mg/L); canine haptoglobin assays are in routine use (CB058, CB232, CB476 and others in grid F1-03); haemopexin seen only by proteomics in dogs (CB117, CB476), and a validated canine haemopexin immunoassay was not verified here. A prospective test is feasible, but archived serum would need a haemolysis index.

verdict_reason: The gap stands: no CB article relates measured cell-free haemoglobin or haem load to outcome in natural canine babesiosis, the human evidence (falciparum, knowlesi, sepsis) agrees, and canine assays exist. The programme's 'weak convergent support' does not hold. DS02 is a pure parasite-load effect that CB082 already reports. DS07 haemoglobin beta partly restates the label, cannot be put per unit of anaemia, moves with another red-cell protein (sample haemolysis not excluded), drops below significance when adjusted for lactoferrin or CD14 or when the top 3 dogs are removed, and has q 0.133. So T04 should be cited as a literature gap, not as a data signal.

human_counterpart.claim: Severe falciparum malaria patients with AKI have higher plasma cell-free haemoglobin; cfHb correlates with parasite burden
Haemin and cell-free haemoglobin at presentation associated with mortality, and haemopexin lower, in Ugandan children with severe malaria
Cell-free haemoglobin increased in proportion to severity in knowlesi malaria and associated with parasitaemia
Higher plasma cell-free haemoglobin independently associated with in-hospital death in sepsis (OR 1.078 per unit)

canine_parallel_already_made: partly: no quantified cfHb-vs-outcome study, but CB082 already reports higher plasma haemoglobin with the higher, more severe dose (the DS02 indicator), CB119 proposes cfHb as a severity measure without data, CB040 and CB119 report the very poor prognosis of haemoconcentrated cases with obvious haemolysis, CB325 and CB412 measured free serum haemoglobin without a severity contrast, and CB157 reports a canine null for free haemoglobin vs azotaemia (B. canis)
